LASA has served the Pierce County community since 1989 when houses of worship came together to see how they could work together and create a safety net for those that were facing eviction or loss of their home due to housing insecurity. They found that many of those needs required minimal intervention at the time such as one-time rental assistance or mortgage payment or help with their utilities or other one-time needs. It soon became apparent however that housing for those experiencing homelessness was also needed. The goal of LASA was at that time and continues to be to use housing assistance as a tool along with case management to keep the family housed. Today LASA houses from 50 to 75 families each year through several housing programs that include emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, both permanent supportive housing and permanent low-income housing. We also continue to provide case management, emergency rental and utility assistance and other services. Also during this time of COVID we're proud that LASA was called upon by the cities of Tacoma, Lakewood and Fife to distribute 1.5 million dollars in the form of emergency rent payment and we were honored to participate and assist our community in this way. While LASA is in the process of acquiring land with the intent of increasing the amount of housing we're able to offer, today we come to you to let you know of our desire to increase the footprint of our client services center. This will enable LASA to expand services to the homeless population in our community through providing a place to shower, to do their laundry and to get out of the heat or cold during bouts of extreme weather. LASA's desire is to be there to provide services to help homeless individuals maintain their dignity and get back off the street as quickly as possible.
